summary: This room is five under-reached citizens, and the shape repeats: three of the five (No Mind Checks Itself, Reflective Practice, Return Ceremony) already point outward to every one of their hop1 neighbors, but almost none of those neighbors point back — a generous-outward, unreached-inward pattern rather than genuine isolation. The fix in each case was quote-backed: a neighbor's own body already names the target in the same terms the target uses about it (Reflective Practice's "the Dialectic at the moment the question itself gets reframed," Return Ceremony's "the two ceremonies are bookends on one organ"), so wiring the reverse link closes a real gap rather than inventing one. Two targets (ELDER, SCHEMA — Reference) had the opposite problem: operational cards that name them by disk path in working prose (Substrate Skill's "read [[ELDER]], then [[SCHEMA]]"; Deposit Ceremony's "read SCHEMA.md and SCHEMA — Reference.md on disk") without ever registering the link. One genuine directional error surfaced along the way — No Mind Checks Itself exemplifies Bring In a Bigger Mind, but the entry itself is the general theoretical wall and the practice is the concrete instance built on it, so the arrow reads backward against SCHEMA §4's own directionality invariant. Two targets also carry a stage that no longer matches their body: No Mind Checks Itself and Return Ceremony are both still marked seed despite being fully synthesized, multi-section entries with real cross-domain content and (for Return Ceremony) a documented live failure case — the word-count test in SCHEMA §2 puts both well past seed. On the question this run was actually launched to test: I was dispatched as a child but instructed to read SCHEMA.md and SCHEMA — Reference.md in full before starting, which is normally elder-only material read at the pen. Having §4's directionality invariant and §2's stage table literally in context is what let me catch the exemplifies-direction error and the two stage-drift flags with a specific rule to cite rather than a vague sense that something was off — I'd have likely proposed the link but missed the directional problem, and left both stages alone, without that text loaded. That's one data point, not a controlled comparison, but it argues for the rule Loudon is weighing: a weave worker doing typed-link and stage work needs SCHEMA §2 and §4 in context regardless of whether it has formally "grown up," because the errors this kind of work produces are exactly the kind those two sections exist to prevent.

typed_relations.label: read-before
typed_relations.rationale: SCHEMA's own body already names ELDER as the reason it exists ('This card is... the first thing an agent reads when it grows up ([[ELDER]])') but carries no frontmatter link back to it — the ELDER walk surfaces its own most-cited-in-prose neighbor missing the wire.
typed_relations.evidence: "This card is the what exists — the first thing an agent reads when it grows up ([[ELDER]])." (SCHEMA.md:48-50)

typed_relations.label: prerequisite
typed_relations.rationale: Substrate Skill's own 'Adding to the Palace' section instructs the reader to read ELDER first, in body prose, with no matching frontmatter link — a direct case of a known entry named at a structurally significant spot (an instruction, not a passing mention) going unregistered.
typed_relations.evidence: "Grow before you draft: read [[ELDER]], then [[SCHEMA]], if you have not this session — a child offers the idea; an elder gives it frontmatter." (Substrate Skill.md:37)

typed_relations.source: The Blindspot Is the Surprise Fuel
typed_relations.label: the-unnamed-wall
typed_relations.rationale: No Mind Checks Itself already mirrors this entry one-way ('the-unnamed-wall'); the relation is genuinely symmetric — both entries argue that a voice/mind which cannot name its own limit cannot be caught, checked, or argued with, at different altitudes (embodied voice vs. self-checking model).

typed_relations.label: every-model-including-this-one
typed_relations.rationale: No Mind Checks Itself already cites Meadows's flattest sentence as its opening altitude; Meadows's own forward_vector independently arrives at the identical claim ('I of all people should stay a learner about my own model') — close enough in register that her page's reader should be sent to the entry that generalizes it.
typed_relations.evidence: "My blindspot is that my moral urgency can outrun my model... I of all people should stay a learner about my own model." (Donella Meadows.md:23,28)

typed_relations.rationale: SCHEMA §4's directionality invariant: exemplifies runs concrete-instance → general-class. Here No Mind Checks Itself is the general structural claim and Bring In a Bigger Mind is the concrete practice built on it — the arrow is backward. The link's own label ('the-practice-this-grounds') already says No Mind Checks Itself is the ground the practice stands on, which is what `enables` (precondition → enabled) means, not what `exemplifies` means.
typed_relations.evidence: link object: target: "[[Bring In a Bigger Mind]]" type: exemplifies label: the-practice-this-grounds (No Mind Checks Itself.md:11-13)

typed_relations.label: in-action
typed_relations.rationale: Reflective Practice names the Dialectic by name and quote as one of only three reflection-in-action mechanisms the palace has; Dialectic's own frontmatter has no link back.
typed_relations.evidence: "Three reflect in action: the [[Dialectic]] at the moment 'the question itself gets reframed by the collision'" (Reflective Practice.md:61-62)

typed_relations.label: generalizes-insularity
typed_relations.rationale: Reflective Practice quotes this entry directly to name over-reflection's failure mode (insularity); the source entry does not link back despite being quoted verbatim.
typed_relations.evidence: "[[The Palace Practices on Itself]] § The counter-discipline calls it insularity: 'a chain of good ones, each answering the previous rather than the work.'" (Reflective Practice.md:100-101)

typed_relations.label: studio-side
typed_relations.rationale: Reflective Practice names this entry as the learning-side half of the same gap it and Creative Coach triangulate; Creative Coach already reciprocates the link, Objects to Think With does not.
typed_relations.evidence: "the teaching-side route to the gap [[Objects to Think With]] reaches from the learning side and [[Creative Coach]] from the coaching side." (Reflective Practice.md:114-116)

typed_relations.label: the-other-bookend
typed_relations.rationale: Return Ceremony's central architectural claim is that it and Closing Well Ceremony are the two bookends of one organ; Closing Well Ceremony's own frontmatter has no link acknowledging this from its side.
typed_relations.evidence: "The Return and the Close are one organ, pointed at opposite boundaries... The two ceremonies are bookends on one organ: summoned at the return, takes the wheel at the close." (Return Ceremony.md:57,63)

typed_relations.label: writing-rules
typed_relations.rationale: Deposit Ceremony's own body sends its reader to SCHEMA — Reference by disk path — the exact 'writing rules read at the pen' the file's own forward_vector describes — but only SCHEMA is registered in frontmatter, not SCHEMA — Reference.
typed_relations.evidence: "If you need the vocabulary yourself, read `SCHEMA.md` and `SCHEMA — Reference.md` on disk." (_ops/Deposit Ceremony.md:50)
